I farm 10.1 mu with a wheat-maize rotation, and I have well irrigation, so I will stay with the system I know best and manage both crops steadily rather than taking risks. I am 66, my household labor is limited, and some family members work off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple, practical, and based on what is dependable in Quzhou. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put on enough nitrogen for stable tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus and some potassium, irrigate at the key times, and control pests and diseases only when needed. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care most about stable yield, then I will fertilize a bit heavily on nitrogen, keep phosphorus and potassium in the plan, use fewer irrigation times than wheat but still water at the important stages, and keep pesticide use moderate. On the tillage side, I will use rotary tillage where it helps me manage residue and sow evenly, but I will keep maize simpler after wheat so the turnover is fast. My goal is stable production and manageable labor, not chasing the highest possible yield.
